reason: The cited evidence shows that remelting strategies can control dislocation density and microstructure in SS316L (E1) and that single-pass laser cladding of AlCoCrFeNi HEA can produce defect-free surfaces (E2), but neither passage provides specific support for the key premises that remelting reduces thermal gradients, homogenizes HEA microstructure, or directly improves dimensional precision and mechanical properties in additively manufactured HEAs.
premises: Laser remelting of a deposited layer reduces residual thermal gradients
Laser remelting promotes microstructural homogenization in HEAs
Reduced thermal gradients and homogenization decrease porosity and defects
In-situ remelting improves dimensional precision in AM components
In-situ remelting enhances mechanical properties (strength, ductility) in AM HEAs
